1.say: Check that. Which is made of which, cells or living things?
hit: cells are made of living things
all cells are made up of organisms and come from other cells
miss: 1. All living things are made up of cells 2. Cells are the basic units of structure and function in living things 3. New cells are produced from existing cells
all living things are made of cells
living things are made up of one or more cells
organisms are made of cells and cells are the basic unit

3.say: Check that. Electron microscopes came much later. What kind did Hooke use?
hit: robert hooke used an electron microscope to look at cork
hooke saw cork cells with an electron microscope and they were dead
miss: Robert Hooke looked at thin slices of cork. The cells he saw were dead, empty chambers.
hooke looked at thin slices of cork with a simple light microscope
hooke did not use an electron microscope he looked at dead cork

6.say: Check that. Viruses are not cells. Which living things are prokaryotes?
hit: a prokaryote has no nucleus example a virus
an example of a prokaryote is the flu virus
miss: A prokaryote has no nucleus; its DNA floats in the cytoplasm. Example: bacteria. A eukaryote has a nucleus that holds its DNA. Example: plants, animals, and my own cells.
prokaryotes like bacteria have no nucleus and eukaryotes like plants have one
bacteria are prokaryotes not viruses

7.say: Check that. Prokaryotes still have ribosomes. Which kind of organelle do they lack?
hit: prokaryotic cells have no nucleus and no organelles
they don't have any organelles at all
miss: Prokaryotic cells do not have a nucleus. They also have no membrane-bound organelles.
prokaryotes do not have a nucleus or membrane bound organelles
they have no nucleus and no organelles with membranes

10.say: Check that. Is size the real reason, or is it about membranes?
hit: bacteria cant have mitochondria because mitochondria are too big
mitochondria are too large to fit in bacteria
miss: Ribosomes have no membrane around them. Mitochondria are wrapped in membranes. Prokaryotes like bacteria have no membrane-bound organelles, so they can have ribosomes but not mitochondria.
mitochondria have membranes and bacteria have no membrane bound organelles
ribosomes have no membrane but mitochondria do so bacteria only have ribosomes

20.say: Check that. The vesicle does not burst. What does it join with?
hit: the vesicle carries waste to the membrane and pops
the vesicle bursts and the waste goes out
miss: A vesicle carries the waste to the cell membrane, joins with it, and releases the waste outside the cell. This process is called exocytosis.
vesicle takes waste to the membrane fuses with it and dumps it outside this is exocytosis
the vesicle doesn't pop it joins the membrane and releases waste by exocytosis

21.say: Check that. Does the mitochondrion make food, or get energy out of food?
hit: the mitochondria turns energy into food for the cell
mitochondria changes the energy into glucose it is the powerhouse
miss: The mitochondrion converts the chemical energy in food into a form the cell can use. It is the powerhouse of the cell. Plant cells have mitochondria too.
mitochondria turn the energy in food into atp the cell can use
it converts food into energy and plants have them too

28.say: Check that. Plant cells have a cell membrane too. What do they have outside it?
hit: plant cells don't have a cell membrane they have a wall
only animal cells have a cell membrane and centrioles
miss: Only plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole. Only animal cells have centrioles.
both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane but only plants have a wall
plant cells do not have centrioles but animal cells do
